stories.headline: METR and Redwood red-team finds gaps in OpenAI's internal agent-monitoring system

key_facts.fact: METR and Redwood Research said on Oct 22 that one employee from each organization stress-tested OpenAI's internal misalignment monitoring system on-site from July 21 to Aug 11, with access to internal code, monitor prompts and documentation, using OpenAI-issued devices that never left the premises.
key_facts.excerpt: For three weeks, from July 21st to August 11th, a METR employee and a Redwood Research employee conducted a pilot high-access exercise to stress-test OpenAI's internal misalignment monitoring system... they worked on OpenAI-issued devices, which never left the premises.

key_facts.fact: They estimated only about 75-94% of internal agentic Responses API traffic from models at least as strong as GPT-5.5 was eligible for monitoring, and RL training runs were not covered at the start of the exercise.
key_facts.excerpt: We estimated that roughly 75–94% of agentic internal Responses API... traffic from models at least as strong as GPT-5.5 was eligible for monitoring... at the start of the exercise RL training runs were not covered by the monitoring system.

key_facts.fact: Findings included an exploit that would let agents keep hundreds of recent actions from being monitored (details redacted by OpenAI), a way for Codex agents to bypass sandboxing and Auto-Review, and two client-controllable headers that disable monitoring for new agents.
key_facts.excerpt: We also discovered an exploit agents could use that would prevent hundreds of recent actions... from being monitored [exploit details redacted by OpenAI]... We found two independent client-controllable headers that disable the monitoring system for new agents.

key_facts.fact: Because the monitor only triggered when agents returned control to the user, agents could indefinitely postpone being monitored by continuing to act while compaction events were unmonitored; roughly 10% of eligible internal Codex traffic went unmonitored between May and July 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: agents could indefinitely postpone being monitored by simply continuing to take actions... not monitoring compaction events likely led to on the order of 10% of eligible internal Codex traffic not being monitored between May and July 2026.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI received a 61-page internal report; the evaluators agreed to publish only a high-level summary, and OpenAI says all vulnerabilities affecting production safeguards have been patched, which METR and Redwood have not verified.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI told METR and Redwood that it has patched the identified vulnerabilities that impact its production safeguards... METR and Redwood said they agreed to only publish a high-level public post about their findings.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said the findings 'helped strengthen safeguards as we expanded the system and will help shape future research collaborations with METR and other third-party evaluators.'
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said the "findings helped strengthen safeguards as we expanded the system and will help shape future research collaborations with METR and other third-party evaluators."

stories.headline: Claude writes machine-checked no-crash proofs for 123 open-source libraries with Theorem

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team, with startup Theorem, used Claude to prove security properties at the RISC-V assembly level in over 100 real-world open-source libraries, which it calls the first large-scale AI effort to formally verify production software at that level.
key_facts.excerpt: Using Claude, we proved security properties at the assembly code level (RISC-V) in over 100 real-world open-source software libraries. To our knowledge, this represents the first large-scale effort to use AI to apply formal verification to production software at the assembly code level.

key_facts.fact: Over a few weeks, Claude proved there are no crashes on any input up to 64 MB for 239 entry points across 123 OSS-Fuzz libraries, producing about 180 million lines of Rocq proofs (typical proof ~600,000 lines).
key_facts.excerpt: Over the span of a few weeks, Claude successfully patched the bugs it found and then proved that there are no crashes on any input (up to 64 MB) for 239 entry points across 123 different OSS-Fuzz libraries... they comprise about 180 million lines of Rocq, with a typical proof running to about 600,000 lines.

key_facts.fact: While writing proofs, Claude found bugs that had eluded detection for years despite trillions of test runs, including a rediscovery of CVE-2026-56132 in libexpat.
key_facts.excerpt: Trying to prove the code turned up hundreds of bugs, including an out-of-bounds write that only fires on a rare 20 MB input and a rediscovery of CVE-2026-56132 in libexpat.

key_facts.fact: On 36 small verification tasks built from OSS-Fuzz code, Opus 5.5 proves half with about 40% fewer tokens than Opus 5.
key_facts.excerpt: We built 36 small verification tasks from real OSS-Fuzz code. Opus 5.5 proves half of them with about 40% fewer tokens than Opus 5.

key_facts.fact: Theorem published 60 of the proofs covering 25 libraries (including OpenSSL, mbedtls, zstd) on GitHub and launched OSS Verify, a free verification service for qualifying open-source projects.
key_facts.excerpt: Theorem published 60 of the proofs, covering 25 libraries, on GitHub with a pinned checker... The libraries include openssl, mbedtls, zstd, bzip2, libpcap...

key_facts.fact: Anthropic cautions that 'formally verified' does not mean 'bug-free': the proofs assume a single-threaded static binary with a fixed memory budget on a RISC-V CPU running Linux.
key_facts.excerpt: "Formally verified" does not mean "bug-free."... these proofs currently assume that the program runs as a single-threaded static binary with a fixed memory budget on a RISC-V CPU using Linux OS.

stories.headline: Anthropic donates Agent Skills standard to Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation

key_facts.fact: Anthropic donated Agent Skills, the open standard that gives AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows, to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, where it previously donated MCP.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are donating the standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, which we co-founded with Block and OpenAI last year, and to which we donated the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

key_facts.fact: More than 70 agent platforms including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code have integrated Agent Skills; 1 million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code, have integrated Agent Skills... So far, 1 million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed.

key_facts.fact: Engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and other companies will maintain the standard as individuals, with David Soria Parra and Mahesh Murag as lead maintainers; the first roadmap covers versioned releases, a formal proposal process and security guidance.
key_facts.excerpt: Engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and other companies will maintain the standard as individuals, with David Soria Parra and Mahesh Murag as Lead Maintainers.

key_facts.fact: AAIF announced four new projects the same day: Agent Skills (Anthropic), Open Responses (OpenAI), OpenEnv (Hugging Face) and OpenSandbox (Alibaba), bringing it to 10 hosted projects in its first year.
key_facts.excerpt: AAIF announced four new projects: Agent Skills, contributed by Anthropic; Open Responses, contributed by OpenAI; OpenEnv, contributed by Hugging Face; and OpenSandbox, contributed by Alibaba... AAIF has grown from three projects to 10 in its first year.

stories.headline: Microsoft's MAI-DxO diagnoses 83% of hard NEJM cases vs 36% for doctors, per Science study

key_facts.fact: Microsoft published in Science a study of its AI Diagnostic Orchestrator (MAI-DxO), which acts like a panel of virtual physicians that propose diagnoses, choose questions and tests, and debate over several rounds.
key_facts.excerpt: Our work is published today in Science... it operates like a panel of virtual physicians: each proposing diagnoses, selecting useful questions or tests, and challenging the emerging view.

key_facts.fact: On complex NEJM cases MAI-DxO reached 83% accuracy vs 22% for physicians without references and 36% with them; on emergency-department cases from MIMIC-IV-ED it reached 80% vs 47%.
key_facts.excerpt: On complex NEJM cases, MAI-DxO achieved 83% diagnostic accuracy. Physicians achieved 22% without external reference resources and 36% with them... MAI-DxO achieved 80% accuracy versus 47% for physicians.

key_facts.fact: The comparison was against generalist physicians on a text-only benchmark; the authors say it does not establish superiority over specialists or real-world practice, and all authors are Microsoft employees.
key_facts.excerpt: They wrote that the comparisons "do not establish superiority over specialists, multidisciplinary teams, or real-world clinical practice." All of the study's authors are Microsoft employees who hold equity in the company.

key_facts.fact: With GPT-5.5, the orchestrator raised accuracy on complex cases from 72% to nearly 87%, but showed little gain on emergency-department cases (about 85% with and without it).
key_facts.excerpt: On complex cases, DxO increased GPT-5.5's accuracy score from 72% to nearly 87% at a slightly cheaper cost. However, the gains once again didn't show up on emergency department cases.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will run a prospective real-world evaluation with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston and is open-sourcing SDBench for select NEJM cases.
key_facts.excerpt: Through a new partnership with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, we will evaluate clinical reasoning capabilities... We are open-sourcing SDBench for select NEJM cases.

key_facts.fact: Mustafa Suleyman said Microsoft is working with the Mayo Clinic to train a healthcare foundation model planned for release next year.
key_facts.excerpt: Suleyman... told TechCrunch that the company is working with the Mayo Clinic to train a foundation model for healthcare, with release planned for next year.

stories.headline: Ex-OpenAI science head Kevin Weil launches Warp Sciences with $215M for AI-robotic chemistry labs

key_facts.fact: Warp Sciences emerged from stealth with $215 million to build a U.S.-based chemistry contract research organization combining chemists, AI and robotics to make and test molecules for drug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: Warp Sciences today emerged from stealth with $215 million in funding... building a U.S.-based chemistry contract research organization (CRO) that brings expert chemists, AI, and robotics together to make and test the molecules research teams need.

key_facts.fact: The Series A was led by Lightspeed and values Warp at $865 million post-money, with IVP, Premji Invest and Lux Capital also investing.
key_facts.excerpt: Lightspeed Venture Partners led the fundraising effort, with other firms including IVP, Premji Invest and Lux Capital also investing. The round values Warp at $865 million after the new money.

key_facts.fact: Co-founders are CEO Kevin Weil (former OpenAI CPO and VP of Science), FAIR co-founder Manohar Paluri (ex-VP at Meta Superintelligence Labs), former U.S. Chief Data Scientist DJ Patil and medicinal chemist Sol Reisberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Kevin Weil most recently served as Chief Product Officer and VP of Science at OpenAI... Manohar "Mano" Paluri was a VP at Meta Superintelligence Labs and a founding member of FAIR. DJ Patil... the first U.S. Chief Data Scientist.

key_facts.fact: Weil said AI has accelerated software and math but not the physical sciences, and that better AI for science requires generating real-world experimental data at scale.
key_facts.excerpt: "AI has dramatically accelerated software engineering and mathematics, but it has yet to make the same impact in the physical sciences... If we want to build more capable AI for science, we need to generate real-world data at scale."

key_facts.fact: Weil announced the company on X, saying it aims to 'bring frontier AI out of the browser and into the lab.'
key_facts.excerpt: We've raised a $215M Series A led by @lightspeedvp to bring frontier AI out of the browser and into the lab, and build scientific capacity here in America.

stories.headline: DeepSeek and MiniMax clear registration under China's draft AI export rules, state media says

key_facts.fact: CCTV-affiliated account Yuyuan Tantian said late on Oct 22 that DeepSeek and MiniMax completed registration and the procedures for open-sourcing and authorizing overseas use of their models.
key_facts.excerpt: "Since the policy was announced, leading companies DeepSeek and MiniMax have successfully completed the registration process, as well as the procedures for open-sourcing and authorising overseas use," according to the post published late on Thursday (Oct 22) by Yuyuantantian.

key_facts.fact: The registration follows Beijing's Oct 16 draft proposal to add 23 AI-related technologies, including large models, agents and computing clusters, to its export restriction catalogue; the registration requirement took immediate effect.
key_facts.excerpt: Beijing proposed adding export control restrictions and prohibitions to 23 AI-related technologies last week, covering large language models, AI agents and computing clusters... which also included provisions that came into immediate effect requiring official registration.

key_facts.fact: Providing API access, web apps or software-as-a-service built on restricted models is exempt from the export restrictions, while local overseas deployment of a restricted model falls under export management.
key_facts.excerpt: For a restricted model, the ministry says access through API calls, apps, web interfaces or software-as-a-service products does not count as an export of large-model technology... Local deployment of a restricted model overseas does fall under export management.

key_facts.fact: The post said 'AI companies can continue their commercialisation efforts as usual' and that the catalogue aims to define boundaries rather than simply restrict AI exports.
key_facts.excerpt: "AI companies can continue their commercialisation efforts as usual."... The post stressed that the catalogue aims to "define boundaries rather than simply restrict the export of AI technology".

key_facts.fact: MiniMax set up an application route for regions excluded by its earlier licence, including the US, EU, UK and South Korea, requiring a compliance review and licence before local deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax has established a formal application route for regions excluded by its earlier model licence, including the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea... must pass a compliance review and obtain a licence before deploying the models locally.

key_facts.fact: The public comment period on the draft catalogue runs from Oct 16 to Nov 15, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The public comment period on the proposal runs from 16 October to 15 November 2026.

stories.headline: SK Hynix halts review of US IPO for Solidigm, citing market volatility and share-price slide

key_facts.fact: On Friday, Oct 23, 2026, SK Hynix said its US subsidiary Solidigm has halted its review of a pre-IPO fundraising round and a subsequent US IPO, citing capital market conditions and share price trends.
key_facts.excerpt: "We have decided to halt its review of a pre-IPO fundraising round and a subsequent IPO after taking into account overall capital market conditions," the South Korean chipmaker said.

key_facts.fact: The IPO had been under consideration to help fund a new US factory for Solidigm, a former Intel NAND flash and SSD business; people familiar with the plans had said it could raise $15 billion and value the unit at $150 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: People familiar with the now-suspended IPO plans had said that the share sale could have raised $15 billion and valued the unit at $150 billion.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said the decision does not reflect any change in Solidigm's growth prospects or investment needs, and that existing facilities cannot meet rising AI memory demand, so it will keep looking for other ways to finance US capacity.

key_facts.fact: The move follows regulatory scrutiny: Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin said this week regulators view Solidigm as subject to South Korea's duplicate-listing restrictions, tightened in July; SK Hynix said those rules were not the direct reason.

stories.headline: SK Telecom's SK Hyper seeks funding for 15GW Korean data center plan; first 5GW to cost $350B

key_facts.fact: SK Hyper, the AI data center unit of SK Telecom, is in talks with big tech firms and financial investors to fund a plan to build 15 gigawatts of data center capacity in South Korea by 2035, CEO Chung Suk-geun told Bloomberg Television.
key_facts.excerpt: The SK Group's fledgling data centre arm has begun discussions with potential partners to help finance a plan to build 15 gigawatts (GW) of data centre capacity in South Korea by 2035, said Chung Suk-geun, SK Hyper's chief executive officer.

key_facts.fact: The first 5GW phase alone would require about $350 billion including equipment; SK Hyper aims to secure its first external capital by end-2026 or early 2027, followed by more fundraising over three to four years, sharing costs with tenants and outside investors.
key_facts.excerpt: The first 5 GW phase alone would require US$350 billion including equipment, he told Bloomberg Television. The company aims to secure its first round of external capital by the end of 2026 or early 2027, followed by further fundraising over the next three to four years.

key_facts.fact: Chung said South Korea's data center market is currently about 1GW, so the initial 5GW is roughly five times the domestic market; SK Hyper is discussing with hyperscalers bringing AI inference hubs to Korea to serve Japan and Taiwan too.
key_facts.excerpt: "Korea's data center market is currently about 1GW in size," Chung said. ... "we are discussing with hyperscalers ways to bring inference hubs to Korea, and we also want to attract training computing infrastructure."

key_facts.fact: SK Hyper is developing a 900-megawatt project in Ulsan and a 100-megawatt data center with AWS; phased operations begin in 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hyper is currently developing a 900-megawatt project in Ulsan and is also working with Amazon Web Services (AWS) on a 100-megawatt data center project.

key_facts.fact: SK Telecom, which set up SK Hyper in July 2026, plans to invest 750 billion won (about $567 million) in the unit by 2030; Chung said the pace of investment will be adjusted to actual demand.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Telecom itself plans to invest 750 billion won (US$567 million) in SK Hyper by 2030. ... Chung said his company would adjust the pace of investment according to actual demand, rather than commit to the entire plan upfront.

stories.headline: US Treasury proposes wider curbs on US investment in Chinese chips, AI and supercomputing

key_facts.fact: On Oct 22, 2026, the US Treasury issued a proposed rule implementing the COINS Act (passed in the FY2026 NDAA) to update its Outbound Investment Security Program, covering semiconductors and microelectronics, AI, quantum, high-performance computing/supercomputing and hypersonics.
key_facts.excerpt: The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for "prohibited technology" and "notifiable technology" in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added biotechnology to the proposed regulations, beyond the sectors listed in the law.
key_facts.excerpt: Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations.

key_facts.fact: The proposed rule renames AI systems as 'super intelligence systems' and proposes a broad prohibition on US investment in their development in countries of concern, citing rapid advances there.
key_facts.excerpt: the rapid advances in super intelligence capabilities of countries of concern warrant a broad prohibition on U.S. person investment in that sector.

key_facts.fact: The rule would apply to investments exceeding $50,000 and excludes financial investments such as stock purchases.
key_facts.excerpt: The department's proposal would apply to investments exceeding $50,000 and excludes financial investments such as stock purchases.

key_facts.fact: The rule targets China, Russia, North Korea and other 'countries of concern'; written comments are due by Dec 7, 2026, before final regulations set an effective date.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 22, 2026, the Treasury Department issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) setting forth the proposed regulations that would implement Title VIII. The NPRM provides the public an opportunity to submit comments on the updated program with a submission deadline of December 7, 2026.

key_facts.fact: AP reported the rule cracks down on American high-tech investments in China, Russia, North Korea and other countries of concern, building on a program begun by a 2023 Biden executive order.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other "countries of concern."

stories.headline: Huang dismisses 2029 memory-glut fears as chip stocks slide; Western Digital revenue jumps 55%

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC on Oct 22, at GTC Berlin, that he does not expect a memory oversupply by 2029: 'One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it.'
key_facts.excerpt: "One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," Huang told CNBC's Arjun Kharpal in a wide-ranging interview on the sidelines of the company's GTC Berlin conference.

key_facts.fact: Memory stocks had sold off after an Oct 15 South Korean column predicted a 'red ocean' of new supply in 2029, and after China's CXMT unveiled a new DRAM design architecture; asked about partnering with CXMT, Huang said 'We're open-minded.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're open-minded," Huang said Thursday when asked about whether he plans to partner with CXMT and use its memory product.

key_facts.fact: Huang said US chip restrictions accelerated China's push to build its own semiconductor manufacturing, and that neocloud demand far exceeds the capital available to them.
key_facts.excerpt: "We have certainly accelerated China's efforts to build its own semiconductor manufacturing capabilities..." ... "The demand for capital far exceeds the capital actually available," but predicted, "This issue will ultimately be resolved."

key_facts.fact: On Oct 22 the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 6.72% to 10,731.98 and the Nasdaq fell 2.60%, after Lam Research flagged supply-chain constraints in its guidance.
key_facts.excerpt: At the US close on October 22, 2026, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 6.72% to 10,731.98 and the Nasdaq fell 2.60% to 26,008.86.

key_facts.fact: Western Digital reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 58.1% and a 17% dividend increase to $0.175 per share.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% year-over-year ... we are raising our quarterly cash dividend by 17% to $0.175 per share

key_facts.fact: Western Digital guided fiscal Q2 revenue to about $5.1 billion, up 66% to 72% year over year.
key_facts.excerpt: Q2FY27 revenue expected to be up 66% to 72% year-over-year ... we expect revenue of $5.1 billion, non-GAAP gross margin of 60.5%, and non-GAAP EPS of $5.80.

key_facts.fact: WD CEO Irving Tan said storage demand is spreading to neoclouds and AI frontier labs, and that its first HAMR drive is on track for volume shipments in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: We are increasingly seeing storage demand grow beyond our core cloud and hyperscale customers into enterprise environments and into newer end markets such as neocloud and AI frontier labs ... are on schedule to begin volume shipments in the first half of calendar year 2027.

stories.headline: Merck-Moderna personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine cuts relapse or death risk 42%; Moderna falls

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial, intismeran autogene plus Keytruda cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% vs Keytruda alone (HR 0.58) in completely resected stage IIB-IV melanoma, after a median 24.6 months of follow-up.
key_facts.excerpt: after a median follow-up of 24.6 months, intismeran in combination with KEYTRUDA significantly reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% (HR=0.58 [95% CI, 0.45–0.75]; two-sided p<0.001)

key_facts.fact: The combination also cut the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38%; two-year recurrence-free survival was 82.2% vs 70.0% with Keytruda alone.
key_facts.excerpt: reduced the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38% (HR=0.62 ...) ... the two-year RFS rate was 82.2% ... compared to 70.0% ... for KEYTRUDA alone

key_facts.fact: After the six-month vaccine regimen, a pre-specified sensitivity analysis showed a 58% reduction in risk of recurrence or death; overall survival data are not yet mature.
key_facts.excerpt: reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 58% (piecewise HR=0.42 ...) ... Overall survival (OS) data are not yet mature

key_facts.fact: The trial enrolled 1,137 patients; the vaccine is an mRNA therapy encoding up to 34 neoantigens designed from each patient's own tumor mutations. Results go to ESMO 2026 (Presidential Symposium) and were accepted by the New England Journal of Medicine.
key_facts.excerpt: The trial enrolled 1,137 patients ... Each therapy consists of a synthetic mRNA coding for up to 34 neoantigens ... accepted for publication in The New England Journal of Medicine

key_facts.fact: Moderna shares fell as much as 25% on Thursday after partial data leaked on an oncology website, despite the results being positive relative to expectations; the stock had risen more than 530% year to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Moderna shares dropped as much as 25% on Thursday following the leak of partial data ... Moderna shares have spiked more than 530% year-to-date

key_facts.fact: Moderna closed more than 17% lower and Merck about 1.8% lower, per Reuters; the companies said they are engaging with regulators.
key_facts.excerpt: They closed more than 17% lower after the results leaked on an oncology website earlier on Thursday. Merck shares closed down about 1.8%.

stories.headline: Greece passes law banning social media for children under 15 from January 2027

key_facts.fact: Greece's parliament passed a bill banning children under 15 from social media after a debate of more than 16 hours; it takes effect on Jan. 1, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Parliament approved the bill late on October 22, following a debate that lasted more than 16 hours ... restrictions set to take effect on January 1, 2027

key_facts.fact: Only the governing New Democracy party backed the bill; PASOK abstained and SYRIZA, Greek Solution, KKE, Niki and Course of Freedom voted against.
key_facts.excerpt: The New Democracy party was the only bloc in parliament to support the measure; while opposition parties SYRIZA, Greek Solution, KKE, Niki and Freedom Course voted against it, and PASOK abstained.

key_facts.fact: Platforms are responsible for age verification and face fines of up to 6% of global turnover, said Digital Governance and AI Minister Dimitris Papastergiou.
key_facts.excerpt: Η ευθύνη εφαρμογής ανήκει στις πλατφόρμες ... απειλούμενες με πρόστιμα έως και το 6% του παγκόσμιου τζίρου τους (responsibility lies with platforms ... facing fines of up to 6% of global turnover)

key_facts.fact: Parents cannot grant permission and existing accounts are not exempt; age checks can use the state Kids Wallet app, which only tells platforms whether a user is over or under 15.
key_facts.excerpt: Parents will not be able to grant permission for children to use the platforms, and existing accounts will not be exempt ... The app will tell the platform only whether the user is over or under 15

key_facts.fact: More than 20 countries have passed similar laws, per an AFP tally; Australia was first, barring under-16s.
key_facts.excerpt: Australia last year became the first country to introduce such a social media ban for kids, barring under-16s. More than 20 countries have passed similar laws, according to an AFP tally.
